html:
The united kingdom of Israel that the Hebrew Bible says David and his son Solomon ruled from Jerusalem, in the southern Levant, around 1000 to 930 BCE. The map draws it in its 1500, 1000 and 700 BCE snapshots, though by the Bible's own dates it existed only around the middle one.

In the biblical story David made Jerusalem his capital, and Solomon built the First Temple there and traded with Hiram, king of the Phoenician city of Tyre. After Solomon died the kingdom split into Israel in the north and Judah in the south (Israel and Judah).

How large and real this kingdom was is one of the most argued questions in biblical archaeology. Few remains of a large state from this time have been found. The Tel Dan stele, from the 800s BCE, mentions the "House of David", which shows that a dynasty claimed him as founder. Some scholars see a real but small chiefdom in the hills of Judah. The northern kingdom later fell to Assyria in 722 BCE, and Judah to Babylon in 586 BCE.
